title: Read time series and their display options (preview)

blocks.content: Explore time series panels on Grafana Play to see how each one shows change over time and what its display options change.

blocks.title: Read a value at a time

blocks.content: Open the **Sample Website Dashboard**.

Four of these panels are time series: **Memory / CPU**, **logins**, **server requests**, and **client side full page load**. Each one answers the question: How has this value gone up and down over time?
Focus on the **server requests** panel.
Time runs along the horizontal axis and the number of requests up the vertical axis. The legend tells the two series apart.
Hover over the graph to read a timestamp and one series' value in the tooltip. Move to a later time and follow the same series to see whether it rises or falls.
A time series needs timestamped numeric values. A stat would reduce these values to one number and hide the pattern.
Open the **Time series graphs** dashboard on its **More Examples** tab.
Find **Lines** in the **Styles** row.
Now notice **Points**. It draws the same kind of data as dots.
Then view **Bars**. The same data again, drawn as bars.
Only the style changes. The timestamped values behind it don't.
Explore panels that differ in one display option to see what interpolation, fill opacity, and stacking change.
Open the **Time series graphs** dashboard on its **More Examples** tab.
Find **Linear** in the **Interpolation** row.
Straight lines join the points.
Notice **Smooth**.
Curves join the points instead. The curves don't add measurements between them.
View **Step before**.
The line is drawn as steps between points. It stays level, then jumps straight up or down to the next value.
Focus on **Lines** again. Its fill opacity is 0, so there is no shading under the line.
Find **Fill opacity = 10**. A faint shade sits under the line.
Select the **Time Series Introduction** tab.
Notice **Simple graph**.
With fill opacity set higher, at 40, the area under each line is shaded heavily. Fill opacity changes only how transparent or solid that shading is. It doesn't change the values the line shows.
View **Simple graph** again. Its **Stack series** option is **Off**.
Hover over the graph. The tooltip shows each series' own value, and each line's height is that value, counted up from zero.
Focus on **Stacked lines**. Its **Stack series** option is **Normal**.

Hover over this graph. Each series is drawn on top of the one below it, so the top line shows their total, not the top series' own value.

Be cautious with stacking. Only the bottom series starts from zero. Each line above it starts where the one below ends, so a line can rise because the series under it grew, not because its own value did.
